item.title: Iran and Israel: Why Aggressor and Defender Are Not Symmetrical
item.description: When a war breaks out, the easiest and most flattering reflex is to declare both sides equally guilty. But moral symmetry between Iran and Israel is a falsehood, and facts, not feelings, are what determine political truth.

item.title: Confronting Personified Evil: The Logic of Eliminating a Dictator
item.description: There are rare moments when global evil concentrates in a single human body. Eliminating such a figure can be a legitimate way to end a war — but the deciding factor is political will, and the only thing that manufactures that will, or forbids it, is the deterrent the man stands behind.

item.title: Ignore the Bluff: Why Nuclear Blackmail Is the Aggressor's Empty Card
item.description: Russia's nuclear threats are not a doctrine but a performance, and the only rational policy toward them is to ignore them. A dictator obsessed with his own survival, a doctrine repeatedly rewritten on paper, and a long ledger of red lines crossed without apocalypse all point to the same verdict: the card is empty, and the West's self-deterrence is a gift to the blackmailer.

item.title: Communicating Vessels: The Dictators' Single War
item.description: We file the world's wars in separate folders — Ukraine here, the Middle East there, North Korea's menace somewhere else. That filing is the mistake. They are fronts of one diffuse war waged by an axis of dictatorships and terror states that behave like communicating vessels: pressure released on one rises on another.
